author: E. J. Logue
title: University Libraries digitize Nevada Silver & Blue magazine archives
text:
The University Libraries’ digital services department announced on May 13 a collaboration with University Advancement to digitize and preserve “Nevada Silver & Blue,” the University’s alumni magazine. The project resulted in the digitization of 209 past issues, spanning from 1972 to the present, which are now available online.
Christy Jerz, University Advancement director of marketing and communications and editor in chief of Nevada Silver & Blue, said, “For more than fifty years, Nevada Silver & Blue has told the stories of the University and the people who shape it. Until now, that rich history had never had a permanent digital home. Digitization expands access for Nevada alumni and friends, ensuring these moments continue to live on.”
The newly digitized collection adds to other campus publications already available through the University Archives. Katherine Dirk, manager of the Libraries’ Digital Services digitization lab, led a team including two student assistants who began scanning issues in Summer 2025 and completed work by Spring 2026. Dirk said, “The magazine feels like a love letter to campus. From campus events and new buildings opening over time, this collection shows how campus has grown, shows what professors were doing, and how visually different campus has looked over the years.”
Several library teams contributed throughout each stage: selecting physical copies from collections based on their condition; using specialized book scanners; generating searchable PDFs through optical character recognition; attaching descriptive metadata; and performing quality control checks before making files accessible online. Dirk described this process as “the hidden work of the library,” emphasizing its complexity: “In order to see things like this online, it takes several Libraries teams and several student assistants to complete this specific loop: Scanning. Coding. Ingesting. Display online. Searchable. Findable… They don’t realize how much work goes into adding objects to the Digital Archive.”
Since 2004, University Advancement has published Nevada Silver & Blue while maintaining its legacy for future generations.
Jerz concluded by saying: “We’re deeply grateful to the University Libraries team whose expertise and behind‑the‑scenes work made it possible to preserve and share this history so thoughtfully and completely.”
